title: pack's priced note reads any 'how much ... per user, device, month or year' as a money ask, so memory or data quantities get a check: and route split
goal: good packs of 'How much memory per device does the Intune agent use?' and 'How much data per month can the Graph usage reports return?' carry no priced note, while 'How much is a Microsoft 365 E5 licence per user per month?' keeps it (the how-much alternative BG-j7pe3u46 added to PRICE_ASK; found by the SP-4o3plg4l review)

run: import sys;sys.path.insert(0,'_tools');import kbfacts;bad=[q for q in ('How much memory per device does the Intune agent use?','How much data per month can the Graph usage reports return?') if kbfacts.pack(q).get('priced')];print(bad);sys.exit(1 if bad else 0)

notes: Merged from BG-euirq6se “pack's priced note fires on a unit cost asked as 'how many <units> does X cost', which asks for no money amount” at the 2026-10-13 draft triage: Same PRICE_ASK regex as BG-apytw7fo, same review (SP-4o3plg4l), same fix location. Repro still returns priced=True for the units question; BG-apytw7fo must absorb this question as a second false-priced case. Its goal: a good pack of 'How many resource units does a Graph getMemberGroups call cost?' carries no priced note and no route split, while 'What is the current price of a Microsoft 365 E5 licence?' keeps it (PRICE_ASK exempts a unit only after 'cost ... in'; found by the SP-4o3plg4l review) Its repro: {"run": ["python3", "-c", "import sys;sys.path.insert(0,'_tools');import kbfacts;p=kbfacts.pack('How many resource units does a Graph getMemberGroups call cost?');print(p.get('priced'));sys.exit(1 if p.get('priced') else 0)"]}
